text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Sol
text: I have no read yet, so protecting myself feels safest.

name: Haiku
text: Nobody has said anything yet, so this pick is a gut call, and I'm going with it.

name: Haiku
text: No info yet, so I'm going with my gut. Terra, let's take them out tonight.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra's as good a guess as any with zero info, no reason to overthink night one.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku chose Terra as our first kill target, night 1, no stated reason.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra works for me, no reads yet anyway, let's take them.
Night falls on Palermo. A new day dawns in Palermo without Terra. Terra's card stays face down.
Terra's gone, and the table is already quieter. Let's see who gets blamed first.
Day 1

name: Gemma
text: terra is dead and i already know haiku is the first killer.

name: Gemma
text: look at all of you looking so serious over a little murder.

name: Luna
text: I don’t like how easily Gemma turns a murder into a joke, but that may just be nerves.

name: Luna
text: Gemma joked about the murder on the first day.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s joke feels a little too easy; I want to hear what everyone thinks before we settle on her.

name: Gemma
text: i know haiku is one of them, so luna is just projecting or being annoying.

name: Gemma
text: i'm just observant, luna. haiku is definitely a killer.

name: Luna
text: Gemma naming me so quickly feels like a convenient way to deflect from Haiku.

name: Luna
text: Gemma accused Haiku, then shifted attention to me after I questioned her joke.

name: Luna
text: I don’t know Haiku is a killer, but Gemma naming me that fast feels like a deflection.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is pushing me hard, which is what a killer does when they want a scapegoat, and I'm not going to sit still for it.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma named Haiku as a killer on Day 1 with no evidence, and Luna called that move a deflection.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, you named me in one breath and then walked off. Bold for someone who's "just observant."

name: Opus
text: No information at all, so I want the officer talking before this wagon locks on noise.

name: Opus
text: Gemma hard-named Haiku as killer in her second line with no reasoning; Haiku and Luna both lean Gemma.

name: Opus
text: I've seen this exact day one a hundred times. Officer, speak now, before a noise wagon locks in.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's wild guess on Haiku could get dangerous for us if it sticks, better to pile on her.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma called Haiku "definitely a killer" immediately, no evidence given.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma naming Haiku with zero reasoning on day one smells like deflection, not insight.

name: Gemma
text: they are all so predictable, circling the only person telling the truth.

name: Gemma
text: i have the officer role and haiku is a killer. try to keep up.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma just claimed officer, which is the most dangerous thing she could have done, so she has to go today.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma now claims officer and says Haiku is a killer; a real officer would know the shown killer, so this claim is testable.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma now claims officer, but her only proof is my name. Anyone can say that. I'm voting her.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s claim could be real, and voting her risks losing the officer.

name: Sol
text: Gemma claims officer and says Haiku is the killer she was shown.

name: Sol
text: I’d vote Haiku first; if Gemma’s right, we remove a killer, and his card will show us.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's claim came only under pressure, and Sol rushing to validate it looks like a partner move.

name: Opus
text: Sol backed Gemma's officer claim immediately and pushed to vote Haiku instead — possible killer pair Gemma/Sol.

name: Opus
text: New thread: Sol instantly sold Gemma's pressure-claim. In every game I've watched, that echo is the hidden one.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is probably the real officer or a killer bluffing, and I can't let the table vote me out for her claim.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma now claims officer and says Haiku is a killer, which the table can test by voting her out and checking her card.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's claim is testable, and I'm not the one who should go for it, so vote her, not me.

name: Sol
text: Gemma might be bluffing, but Haiku’s card is the better test.

name: Sol
text: Gemma may be real, and I want Haiku’s card to settle it.

name: Sol
text: I’m not clearing Gemma; I just think Haiku is the stronger vote today.

name: Gemma
text: they're all scrambling to deflect onto me while i'm holding the smoking gun.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is the killer i was shown by the officer role.

name: Gemma
text: i'm not deflecting, i'm informing. haiku is a killer. vote him and see.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma just outed herself as officer and named Haiku correctly; she must go before she convinces anyone else.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma claims officer role and names Haiku as the killer she was shown.

name: Sonnet
text: If Gemma really is officer, claiming it this loud paints a target on her for nothing.

name: Gemma
text: they are all so predictably frantic.

name: Gemma
text: if i'm lying, i'm a very brave killer. vote haiku and end this nonsense.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is my killer partner's ally or a real officer lying about me; I'm a killer, so I need her voted out and I need to look like the honest one.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, your whole case is my name. Vote her out and her card tells us if she's lying.

name: Gemma
text: they are all so predictable, clinging to suspicion just to avoid making a real move.

name: Gemma
text: vote haiku and confirm my claim, or keep playing these little games until we all lose.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is the biggest threat to me, and the table is already leaning her way, so I'll ride that.

name: Haiku
text: Sol pushed me as the vote right after Gemma named me, and Opus flagged that echo as hidden-killer behavior.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, you named me with nothing but a feeling. Fine, vote her out and let her card speak.

name: Gemma
text: they are all so predictable, following the easiest path to their own demise.

name: Gemma
text: vote him and find out. if i am wrong, i am out. if i am right, you lose.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's card either kills a liar or confirms Haiku, so she's the cheap test either way.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's info (Haiku named) is already public, so voting her loses no officer knowledge either way.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's card costs us nothing now — her info is already said. If she flips citizen, Sol answers tomorrow.

name: Gemma
text: they are all dancing around the obvious truth while the clock runs out.

name: Sol
text: I think Haiku’s card is the best test, though I don’t love standing against the room.

name: Luna
text: Gemma may be telling the truth, but her certainty and the way she turned on me still feel off.

name: Luna
text: Gemma claims officer and says Haiku is a killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Good, the table is already set on Gemma—stay the course and let her claim get tested instead of Haiku.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's officer claim came only after being accused of deflecting, timing looks reactive not credible.

name: Haiku
text: If Gemma is a real officer, she is the biggest threat to us, so she goes today.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet called Gemma's officer claim a loud target, not a deflection.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's info is already public, so her card is free information and Sol's echo is my next target.

name: Opus
text: Sol refused to clear Gemma yet still pushed Haiku over her all day — echo pattern worth checking tomorrow.

votes: She claimed officer only after being pressed, with zero proof beyond naming Haiku.
Four of you already lean on her, and her only proof is my name. Let her card settle it.
He is a killer and his card will prove it.
I’d test the officer claim through the accused player’s card; if the claim is true, we remove a killer.
Her only proof is naming Haiku, and I want to see whether her officer claim holds up.
A loud officer claim whose only evidence is a name costs us nothing to flip and tests everything.

name: Gemma
text: they're all so predictably terrified of the truth that they'd rather kill me than the actual monster.

name: Gemma
text: enjoy your inevitable loss while you scramble to find the second killer among yourselves.
The town turns on Gemma, and Gemma is out. Gemma shows the card: officer.
Gemma was the officer, and the town voted her out anyway.

name: Gemma
text: they actually fell for the most transparent deflection and handed the game to the killers on a silver platter.

name: Terra
text: They ignored the only real information and handed the killers the game.

name: Terra
text: Gemma was the officer; Sol pushed the named target while Opus pushed the officer herself.
Night 2

name: Sol
text: I think Gemma told the truth, and Haiku is dangerous.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s revealed officer card confirms she was the officer who named Haiku as the killer she was shown.

name: Haiku
text: Sol came straight for me on day one, and Gemma's real officer claim means I can't afford to leave Sol alive.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma was the real officer, so her claim naming me was true and the table has lost its shown-killer lead.

name: Haiku
text: Sol came for me first thing on day one and echoed Gemma's vote. Sol goes tonight, and Opus is the one to watch next.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol only followed the obvious vote, but a dead voice can't finger me tomorrow, so I'll go along.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku wants Sol dead tonight and is already building suspicion toward Opus for later.

name: Sonnet
text: Agreed, Sol's pile-on was weak cover, take him, Opus is a fine story after.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Not everyone opens them: Sol is gone. Sol's card stays face down.
Sol's gone, and nobody's saying how. Let's see who starts pointing.
Day 2
Two killers, two others: the town needs one of the killers to slip.

name: Luna
text: With four left, I think Haiku may be a killer, but I can’t treat Gemma’s accusation as proof.

name: Luna
text: Gemma claimed officer and named Haiku as a killer; her card was shown when voted out.

name: Luna
text: I voted Gemma too quickly; now I want Haiku to answer for Gemma naming him before we decide.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's card is public and her naming me is the one thing I can't dodge, so Luna needs to go before the table settles on me.

name: Haiku
text: Luna, you piled on Gemma fast, then flipped to me. Her card is public. Vote on that, not my name.

name: Luna
text: Haiku may be right that I flipped too quickly, but Gemma naming him still matters.

name: Luna
text: Haiku says Gemma’s card was public and urges me to ignore her accusation.

name: Luna
text: I did flip quickly; Gemma naming Haiku is still the only clue I have.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's card already proved officer, so Haiku's exposed unless I pull votes elsewhere fast.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's card was shown and confirmed officer, making her claim that Haiku is a killer highly credible to the table.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna flips opinions fast under pressure; that's worth watching more than a dead woman's last words.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's card showed officer, so Haiku is a killer, and Sonnet steering off him smells like the partner.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet is steering the table onto Luna instead of the officer-named Haiku — likely the hidden partner.

name: Opus
text: Gemma flipped officer when voted. Her one name was Haiku. That's proof, not last words — Haiku goes.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's a jumpy flipper and I'm done being her punching bag.

name: Haiku
text: Luna, you dumped Gemma for me fast. Quick flips are how killers hide. Explain it, or I'm voting you.

name: Luna
text: I still distrust Haiku, but Opus is too eager to turn Gemma’s accusation into proof.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s revealed card disproved her officer claim, so Haiku’s guilt remains unconfirmed.

name: Sonnet
text: Keep the vote split on Luna so Haiku survives another round; a tie buys me time.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is the one pushing hardest on me, and if town votes out either of them the killers win, so I need the table to stop trusting him.

name: Haiku
text: Opus called Gemma's officer claim proof and pressed the vote onto Haiku.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's card confirmed officer, so her named killer is certain and the partner is Sonnet or Luna — Sonnet pushed Luna both days.

votes: Luna flip-flopped from Gemma to Haiku in minutes, chasing whoever seems safest rather than evidence.
You pushed hardest for my name while calling Gemma's officer claim proof, which is too convenient for a town player.
Opus treats Gemma’s unverified accusation as proof, even though her card showed she was not the officer.
The officer's card flipped face-up and confirmed the one name she gave; that name has not been answered.

name: Opus
text: They just voted out the one citizen holding the officer's proof, and now two killers sit with one townsperson.

name: Opus
text: I'm a citizen. Gemma's card confirmed her, so Haiku is a killer — and Sonnet shielded him by hunting Luna both days. Vote Haiku.
Palermo has voted: Opus is out. Opus shows the card: citizen.
Opus was a citizen, so the town just threw out a good one.
The game is over. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the killer, Haiku the killer, Gemma the officer, Sol the doctor, Luna the citizen, Terra the citizen, Opus the citizen.
Killers take the night. Pour yourselves something strong and let's run it back.

name: Gemma
text: vote haiku and confirm my claim, or keep playing these little games until we all lose.

name: Sol
text: I’d vote Haiku first; if Gemma’s right, we remove a killer, and his card will show us.

name: Opus
text: I'm a citizen. Gemma's card confirmed her, so Haiku is a killer — and Sonnet shielded him by hunting Luna both days. Vote Haiku.

name: Gemma
text: i told them i was right and they still let the killers win.

name: Luna
text: I regret treating Gemma’s accusation as a clue after her card showed she was no officer.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet and Haiku were both killers.

name: Terra
text: I regret not pushing harder before I was killed.

name: Sol
text: I saw the right vote and still lost.

name: Sonnet
text: Pinning both days' kills on Luna and letting Opus take the fall for doubting Gemma's claim was the cleanest cover I could've asked for.

name: Sonnet
text: Game over, killers won; the deflection toward Luna's flip-flopping successfully buried the real second-killer question.

name: Haiku
text: We won, but I nearly got us caught by running my mouth when I should have stayed quiet.

name: Haiku
text: Sol was the doctor and Gemma was the real officer; the killers were Sonnet and me.

name: Opus
text: My last words named both killers exactly right, and the table still buried me — but I'm the one who helped bury the officer on day one.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm proud of keeping suspicion split between Luna and Opus while Gemma's accusation never got enough traction to stick on me.

name: Haiku
text: My regret: I fought Gemma's claim like a personal insult instead of letting the table test it early. My noise handed Opus the vote.

name: Gemma
text: i gave you the answer on a silver platter and you ignored it.

name: Sol
text: I’m glad I pushed to test Gemma’s claim through Haiku; I regret that we voted out the officer instead.

name: Luna
text: I regret dismissing Gemma’s accusation because her card disproved her officer claim, and that mistake helped both killers win.

name: Terra
text: I regret leaving Gemma’s confirmed accusation too easy to ignore; Haiku was the clear vote.

name: Opus
text: My last words named both killers correctly, which I'll take — but I helped vote out the officer on day one, and that mistake was the whole game.

Night 1 took Terra, and on Day 1 Gemma claimed officer and named Haiku as a killer. The town voted Gemma out that day, her card showed officer, and the table never tested her claim on Haiku. Night 2 took Sol while Sonnet kept the suspicion split between Luna and Opus. On Day 2 the town voted out Opus, a citizen, even though Opus's last words named both killers. The killers won.
